transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I wanted to get us together to discuss the Atlas toolkit release scheduled for next Friday. As we all know, the engineering team plans to publish it in our public repository, and it includes source code, documentation, and a sample training package for external developers. Before I can give my final legal approval and record it in the release ticket, I need to make sure we've completed all the pre-release conditions across the board. So I'd like to hear from each of you -- open-source, commercial, export-control, and privacy -- on where we stand with the checklist update for this weekly product-release legal gate. What's the current status from your respective areas?

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical open-source issue. While reviewing the build manifest this week, I confirmed that the public distribution links the Atlas toolkit with a GPLv3 library. This means the combined distribution must use the GPLv3 license and include corresponding source and attribution notices. I have not yet updated the release ticket with this finding, so this pre-release condition remains outstanding from the open-source side.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical commercial issue. I reviewed our largest customer's source-code agreement and confirmed that the customer's proprietary connector is included in the current build of the Atlas toolkit. That agreement prohibits public release of the connector without written customer consent. This means the public package must exclude the connector, be limited to the core toolkit, and document the exclusion in the release checklist. I have not yet added this contract restriction to the release checklist, so this pre-release condition remains outstanding from the commercial side.
